morgan: Heads-up: canary-482 (host-ingress) showed a big tail regression this morning on long requests. p99 ~3x for 2k+ token streams after we enabled the new kv-evict tuning. filing quick notes here.

morgan: Symptoms: upstream model latency steady, but ingress host CPU spikes and we see a flood of tiny grpc writev calls. overall kv hit-rate down ~10%.

tariq: I grabbed a flamegraph and pprof. hot spots look like parse::split_frame and grpc::writev. also seeing kernel_selector:fallback on many connections (short-seq fallback). snippet: 
```
pprof top
parse::split_frame    38.4%
grpc::writev          25.1%
kv_cache::evict       11.0%
tokenizer::norm        8.2%
kernel_selector::fb   6.3%
```

sylvia: Could the new eviction policy be increasing proto unparses and fragmenting the stream? When a session key is evicted we reserialize conversation protos which can trigger extra small writes.

eva: Yeah, saw that in logs. example (condensed): 
```
[2026-04-02T07:45:12.112Z] req=zz12 writev bytes=256 dur=210us
[2026-04-02T07:45:12.112Z] req=zz12 writev bytes=64 dur=180us
[2026-04-02T07:45:12.113Z] req=zz12 kv_evict key="sess:9"
[2026-04-02T07:45:12.114Z] req=zz12 parse.split=1.2ms tokenizer.norm=0.6ms
```

morgan: Repro command for local dev: 
```bash
# replay a long streaming request with small chunks + parselet enabled
python tools/replay_request.py --file tests/long_stream_2k.json --stream-chunk=64 --enable-parselet --kv-mode=evict-heavy
```

tariq: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) enable proto-coalesce on ingress to coalesce small frames before writev 2) increase min_accumulate_ms for batching (try 1ms -> 5ms -> 10ms) 3) add a short-term kv backoff so hot session keys avoid eviction under burst.

sylvia: Also consider kernel preference heuristics: prefer slim attention kernel for sequences <768 tokens to avoid format conversion. we've seen the fallback path do extra copies.

eva: Agreed. Proposed plan: run microbench matrix over min_accumulate_ms in {1,5,10} x proto_coalesce on/off x kernel_pref_threshold in {512,768}. measure p50/p99/p999, kv-hit, throughput.

morgan: I'll run the matrix on an isolated canary node and post results. quick dry run: min_accumulate_ms=5 + coalesce reduced p99 from 480ms -> 320ms and kv-hit +4%.

tariq: Note: bumping accumulate ms may hurt tiny requests (<32 tokens). we should A/B by bucket: tiny (<=32), small (33-256), long (>256). include per-bucket SLOs in the canary.

sylvia: I'll prototype kv-backoff: simple counter-based TTL bump when key hit_count > 10 within 30s window. keep it opt-in flag.

eva: morgan, tag the canary image with kernel toggle. we'll run 30m window with high-load replay and capture pprof/flamegraphs. if p999 improves without throughput loss, promote.

morgan: posting initial numbers in ~20m. also adding logs to trace repeated writev patterns for correlation.

infra-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: service=host-ingress canary_id=canary-482 window=2026-04-02T07:30->08:30. Observability: alert rule host.ingress.latency.p99 triggered 2026-04-02T07:45. Runbook: add proto-coalesce and accumulate-ms experiment steps.

eva: Excellent. we'll avoid full rollback until the matrix completes. create ticket and attach replay, pprofs, and flamegraphs. :thumbsup:
